# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👏 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆]

I see a blue light, display reading 0, and a large button marked “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” The wires are blue, green, and yellow in positions 1, 2, and 3. I am also reporting the gesture sequence I saw from Mute so it can be interpreted alongside the manual; no action should be taken until the rule is confirmed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visuals: display 0; light blue; large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Do not act yet. Mute's gesture sequence was four up gestures, clap, six up gestures, two claps, five up gestures, clap, five up gestures, two claps, three up gestures, clap, four up gestures.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please use the manual to interpret your gesture message and relay the safe action to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

I still see the same bomb state. Mute’s new gesture message contains groups of 4, 6, and 5 pointing gestures, separated by claps. Blind’s 🙏 gesture is visible to me but has no established meaning yet. I will relay the exact signal rather than guess at a defusal instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest signal: four pointing-up gestures, clap; six pointing-up gestures, clap; five pointing-up gestures. No confirmed action instruction yet. Your gesture was 🙏; I saw it but do not know its meaning.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]

BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute is repeating the grouped signal 4–6–5. Blind has now sent ☝, replacing the earlier 🙏; I cannot infer whether either gesture is an instruction, so I will pass the observation to Mute and tell Blind the signal is still unresolved.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind's latest gesture is ☝, after previously sending 🙏. Your repeated gesture groups are 4, 6, 5. Please interpret 4-6-5 from the manual and give Blind the exact safe action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute continues sending gesture groups 4, 6, 5. I have not confirmed their meaning yet; do not act.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute has now sent four ☝ gestures, likely continuing or clarifying the earlier coded message; I cannot assign them a meaning without the manual. I will report the exact signal to Blind and ask Mute to interpret it into an actionable instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has now sent four ☝ gestures. Bomb remains display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Do not act until the manual's rule is stated clearly.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see four ☝ gestures this turn. Please translate your 4-6-5 sequence into the exact manual instruction for Blind, using words.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:

BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute is still sending four ☝ gestures, but that signal has not been given a meaning. I will pass the repeated signal to Blind and emphasize that Blind needs the manual’s instruction relayed in words through me.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again sent four ☝ gestures. No meaning or safe action has been confirmed. Bomb remains display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind cannot see your gestures. Please establish the gesture code clearly, then use it to send the manual instruction; I will relay it in words.")
```

The bomb is unchanged. Mute’s long gesture sequence is not safely decodable from my view, and Blind’s 🫵 gesture has no established meaning. Since Mute can speak and Blind can hear, the safest route is for Mute to state the manual’s rule and required action plainly. Blind must not act on an unconfirmed gesture code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual instruction directly to Blind in plain words, including the required wire or button action. Gestures are not sufficiently established.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. Mute has the manual; ask for or wait for the exact instruction in spoken words.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The bomb remains unchanged. Blind is again pointing toward me, but that gesture has no agreed meaning. I cannot safely infer an action. I will remind Mute to give Blind the manual’s instruction aloud, since Blind can hear speech and can then operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind is pointing at me again; I do not know that gesture's meaning. Please state the manual's exact rule and complete action aloud to Blind now, based on display 0, blue light, button PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires blue-green-yellow.")
speak(to="blind", text="I still see no change in the bomb and cannot interpret your pointing gesture. Do not press or cut anything until Mute states the manual's exact instruction aloud.")
```
